dashboard.addBody: Click this button to open the chart library — or click Next and the guide will open it for you.
dashboard.aDeputyBothManagesAnArea: A deputy both manages an area and has their own KPIs, so the default layout includes one unit-level widget and one personal widget.
dashboard.autosaveBody: No Save button needed: the layout is saved when you let go, and Saving / Saved shows here. Each person and role has their own layout.
dashboard.cardBody: Click a card to add the chart to the page, click again to remove it. The "Suggested for you" label marks charts that fit your position.
dashboard.cardTitle: Click a card to add it
dashboard.cellBody: The figures come straight from the Analytics & Statistics page, so both places always match. Hover over a chart to see details.
dashboard.doneBody: Close the library. Everything you added or removed is already saved.
dashboard.dragBody: Hold this dotted handle and drag the tile to a new spot. The other tiles shift to make room.
dashboard.filterBody: Pick the suggestion chip to see only the charts that fit your position; pick All to see every chart.
dashboard.groupsBody: Click a group name to scroll to it. The number shows how many charts the group has.
dashboard.helpBody: You now know the Overview page. Click this button to see the guide again — every screen has its own.
dashboard.menuBody: The ⋮ button has Settings, Copy image, Move up/down, Change width and Remove from page. You can rearrange tiles with this menu without a mouse.
dashboard.presetsBody: Apply a whole ready-made set of charts in one click. You are asked to confirm first, and an Undo button is still offered afterwards.
dashboard.resetBody: Return the page to the default layout for your role. You are asked to confirm before it resets.
dashboard.resizeBody: Drag a corner or edge of the tile to make it bigger or smaller.
dashboard.searchBody: Type a name or description to filter quickly. Feel free to try it now.
dashboard.theHomePageShowsTheKpis: The home page shows the KPIs you hold: trends over time and a detailed table of each KPI — click a row to see all its submissions and scores.
dashboard.unitLevelWidgetsHereFollowThe: Unit-level widgets here follow the scope you manage: the department's progress, who is late, and the ranking of people under you.
dashboard.youSeeBothUnitLevelWidgets: You see both unit-level widgets (KPI trends, performance of each unit, risks, rankings) and your own personal widgets.

DashboardCustomizeChrome.addTheContentYouNeedTo: Add the content you need to track, or use a suggested layout to start quickly.
DashboardCustomizeChrome.chooseByTheGroupOfFigures: Choose by the group of figures you want to answer
DashboardCustomizeChrome.searchChartsByNameOrDescription: Search charts by name or description…
DashboardCustomizeChrome.thisSuggestedSetHasNoCards: This suggested set has no cards.
DashboardCustomizeChrome.yourCurrentLayoutWillBeCompletely: Your current layout will be completely replaced by the default layout. After resetting you can still click Undo in the notification that appears.
DashboardCustomizeChrome.yourCurrentLayoutWillBeCompletely2: {{value}} Your current layout will be completely replaced. After applying you can still click Undo in the notification that appears.

kpiCreate.part2: Create a KPI (2/3): Source and content
kpiCreate.part3: Create a KPI (3/3): Submit for approval
kpiCreate.introBody: The form has three stages: context (period, unit, assignees), KPI source, then content and figures. The guide only opens the form for you to look at; it creates nothing.
kpiCreate.addBody: Click "Create KPI" to open the form — or click Next and the guide will open it for you.
kpiCreate.typeBody: Quantitative KPIs are scored by the figure achieved against the target. Qualitative KPIs have no figure and are scored on the qualitative scale.
kpiCreate.periodBody: A KPI belongs to one period. Periods of a locked cycle are greyed out; the end of the list has a shortcut to create a new period.
kpiCreate.frequencyBody: How often the assignee reports results. The list only offers frequencies no longer than the chosen period type.
kpiCreate.deadlineBody: Leave it empty to use the end date of the period. A custom deadline must fall within the period.
kpiCreate.unitsBody: Click to choose the units that receive the KPI. The chosen units decide who can be assigned and which BSC / OKR applies.
kpiCreate.assigneesBody: Choose the assignees from the chosen units. When staff create their own KPI, the assignee is always themselves.
kpiCreate.assigneeFilterBody: Type a name or email to search, or click a role to show only people with that role.
kpiCreate.sourceBody: Free-form, from a BSC item, or from an OKR key result (KR). Picking a source prefills the target, unit of measure, weight and name.
kpiCreate.sourceBscBody: Choose an item from the unit's BSC scorecard for this period; the figures on the right are the item's target and weight. If the unit has a scorecard for the period, a scored KPI must be linked to an item or a KR.
kpiCreate.sourceOkrBody: Choose a KR under an objective of the chosen unit. The target is prefilled with what the KR still has to achieve.
kpiCreate.reverseBody: Turn on when lower is better, such as error rate or cost. The target field then becomes "Target threshold" and the minimum becomes "Maximum acceptable threshold".
kpiCreate.bonusBody: An optional KPI that is not part of the 100% weight. The weight field then holds bonus points.
kpiCreate.nameBody: Short and clear about what is measured, e.g. "October revenue". The name appears in lists, reports and notifications.
kpiCreate.aiBody: K.AI reads the unit's figures and documents and suggests KPIs. Click Fill on a suggestion to put it straight into this form.
kpiCreate.descriptionBody: Give the context and how it is measured, so the assignee and the approver read it the same way.
kpiCreate.targetBody: The figure to reach. For an inverse KPI this is a threshold — lower is better.
kpiCreate.minimumBody: Below this the KPI counts as not met. For an inverse KPI this is the maximum acceptable threshold.
kpiCreate.unitBody: For example VND, %, customers. It is shown next to every figure of the KPI.
kpiCreate.weightBody: The KPI's share of the assignee's 100% in this period. When linked to a BSC item, this is the weight within the item.
kpiCreate.submitBody: Click to save. If you can approve your own KPIs it is approved at once; otherwise it stays a Draft and must be submitted for approval. While the guide runs, this button creates nothing.
kpiCreate.tabsBody: Draft is not submitted yet; Pending approval is going through the approval chain; Returned needs fixing and resubmitting.
kpiCreate.myDraftsBody: A shortcut to the KPIs you created but have not submitted for approval.
kpiCreate.rowSelectBody: Tick draft KPIs; the bar at the bottom shows a "Submit for approval" button for everything selected.
kpiCreate.personSelectTitle: Select all of one person's KPIs
kpiCreate.personSelectBody: Select every submittable KPI of this person in one click.
kpiCreate.rowMenuBody: The ⋮ menu has Submit for approval. It only works when the assignee's total weight in the period is exactly 100%.
kpiCreate.submitAiBody: K.AI checks the weights and submits the drafts of the selected unit and period for you, after you confirm.
kpiCreate.chainBody: The KPI moves to Pending approval and is approved in turn by the unit heads, from the KPI's unit up to the root. If it is returned, fix it and submit again.
kpiCreate.helpBody: You have walked through the whole KPI creation flow. These three guides are always in the Guide button menu.

intro.b: Three groups: Organization (how many levels the company has), People (who works where and can do what) and System (how the app talks to staff). Click a card to open it.

info.b: Name, business code, logo and the list of enabled features. Usually edited once at setup.

ranks.b: How many levels the company has and what each is called. Settle this before building the unit tree.

org-structure.b: Build the unit tree and assign each unit head. The tree drives the approval chain and who sees whose data.

users.b: Add people and assign their unit and title. Missing either one means they cannot receive KPIs yet.

delegations.b: Let a person also manage units outside their own tree, for a limited time.

roles.b: Roles and their permissions. Give permissions to roles, then roles to people — not one-off permissions.

sidebar.b: Rename menu items and in-page items to match your company terms.

notifications.b: Which events send email, which only ring the bell, and evaluation deadline reminders.

email.b: Edit the subject and body of system emails, per language.

api.b: Connect Lark so staff can sign in with their Lark account.

ai-docs.b: Internal documents K.AI reads when answering questions about the company.

kpi-workflow.b: Turn steps of the organization's KPI flow on or off, shown as a diagram.

cover.b: Click to change the company's cover image. No need to enter edit mode.

logo.b: The logo appears on exported reports and in system emails. Click the camera icon to change it.

edit.b: Opens edit mode for name, industry, tax code, company size and description.

profile.b: These fields are editable only after clicking Edit profile. Click Save at the bottom when done.

features.b: A green dot means the organization uses that module. This block is view-only.

featuresManage.b: To turn modules on or off, click here to go to Tool setup › Modules & features.

list.b: Each row is one level of the unit tree, top to bottom, with the title of the person managing it.

edit.b: Rename, add, remove or reorder levels. Adding or removing levels affects units already created, so settle it early.

stats.b: Total roles, how many the system created, how many are custom, and how many are leadership level.

add.b: Create a role with a name, management tier and position, then pick its permissions.

hierarchy.b: Set permissions shared by every role at the same level, instead of assigning them role by role.

search.b: Type a name or identifier to filter the list.

table.b: Each row shows the position in the hierarchy and whether the role is system or custom.

rowMenu.b: This menu has Permissions, Edit and Delete role. System roles are protected and cannot be deleted.

viewMode.b: The chart shows the overall management flow; the list is for finding and editing quickly.

content.b: Click a unit to edit it, add a child unit or assign the head. A unit without a head blocks its KPI approval chain.

createRoot.b: If the tree is empty, start with the root unit — usually the whole company.

import.b: For a large tree, import it from an Excel file instead of creating units one by one.

export.b: Export the whole tree to Excel to review it or edit in bulk and import again.

add.b: Create a single account and pick the unit and title right in the form.

import.b: For long lists, import from Excel; the dialog has a template with the right column order.

search.b: Type a name or email to find someone quickly.

roleFilter.b: Show only people with one title.

unitFilter.b: Show only the people of one unit.

table.b: Click a row to open the profile. An empty Role or Unit column means the person cannot receive KPIs yet.

rowMenu.b: This menu has Edit profile, Revoke system access and Delete personal documents.

add.b: Pick the person, the extra unit and the period. You can allow them to act as unit head.

note.b: A delegation grants no new permission: someone who cannot finalize a cycle anywhere still cannot after being delegated.

list.b: Each row shows the delegate, from which unit to which unit, and whether it is still in effect. It is empty until you create one.

revoke.b: Click to end the delegation now instead of waiting for it to expire.

header.b: The line under the heading counts renamed items. Renaming changes neither function nor permission.

search.b: Filters by both the default name and the name you set.

note.b: The first block is the sidebar rows; the following blocks are items inside each page.

scope.b: Each row has the default name and a field for the new name. Leave it empty to go back to the default.

resetItem.b: Click to clear the custom name of this item only.

save.b: All fields are saved at once. Leaving the page before saving loses what you typed.

events.b: Each row is one event, with separate Email and System switches. For frequent events, the bell alone is usually enough.

save.b: These settings are the default for every employee. Remember to click Save.

deadline.b: Reminds unit heads before a period or cycle closes if people are still unscored. Set 0 days to turn it off.

language.b: Each language has its own content; recipients get the version in their language.

list.b: Every email the system sends, grouped.

template.b: Click to open that template on the right.

enabled.t: Turn the email on or off
enabled.b: When off, the system stops sending this email. Security emails such as password reset are always on.

notifLink.b: Some emails are switched by the notification settings — click here to go there.

subject.b: Variables such as the recipient's name are filled in when sending. A missing required variable blocks saving.

advanced.b: Switch between visual editing and full HTML without losing content.

preview.b: Renders the email with sample data. Preview before saving — sent emails cannot be recalled.

reset.b: Returns the template to the original. The button is dimmed when the template was never edited.

save.b: Saves the subject and body for the selected language.

status.b: This bar shows whether Lark sign-in is on and which Lark organization is linked.

createApp.b: Requires a Lark admin account: open Lark Developer Console and create a Custom App.

configure.b: Copy the values here into Lark Console, then create a version and publish the app.

credentials.t: Step 3: App ID and App Secret
credentials.b: Found on the Credentials & Basic Info page of the new app; paste them here and save.

test.b: Click to test the App ID and App Secret you just entered.

connect.b: Sign in to Lark once; KeyGo identifies your company and remembers it.

defaults.t: Unit and role for new people
defaults.b: People signing in with Lark for the first time get an account placed here. Pick the narrowest role and raise it later.

enable.b: Once on, your company appears on the company picker and staff can sign in with Lark.

card.b: K.AI reads company documents in the document library when answering questions about rules and processes.

open.b: Goes to the Documents page, Company scope, to add or edit documents.

org.b: Applies to everyone. Without configuration permission you can still view the running flow.

graph.b: Each node is a step. Click a node to see details and turn it on or off; core steps cannot be turned off.

reset.b: Returns the flow to the system default.

save.b: Saving works only when no step dependency warnings remain.

fullscreen.b: Opens the diagram full screen; press Esc to exit.

mine.b: Hide steps from your own screen only. Nothing changes for anyone else.

mineToggle.b: Click to hide this step from your screen, click again to show it.

intro.b: The Configuration group sets scoring rules, set once. The Tools group is the per-cycle work: cycles and periods, OKR, BSC, rewards, wallet, AI. A missing card means the organization has that tool turned off.

modules.b: The master switches: OKR, BSC, behavioral KPIs, cascading, rewards, wallet. New organizations should start here.

scoring.b: Quantitative scale, qualitative levels and conduct criteria sets. Settle them before opening the first cycle.

matrix.b: Combines behavior score and KPI % into each person's final rating.

unit-class.b: Rates a whole unit by the share of people at each level.

code-rules.b: Code patterns for OKR objectives and BSC scorecards.

kpi-cycles.b: Open cycles and periods. Every KPI and submission belongs to a period.

okr.b: Set strategic objectives and the key results that measure them.

bsc.b: Build the company BSC scorecard and cascade it to departments.

rewards.b: Award points, grant budgets, check-ins, certificates and gifts for points.

wallet.b: Employees' real-money wallet: balances, top-up settings and transfer reconciliation.

ai-quota.b: Split K.AI token quota among people.

ai-review.b: AI score suggestions when reviewing submissions, and the criteria AI relies on.

list.b: Turning a module off hides its menu items and related steps. Nothing is deleted; turning it back on brings the data back.

switch.b: Click to turn this module on or off for the whole organization.

details.b: See what the module brings, e.g. turning on BSC adds scorecard setup and the BSC view in Statistics.

tabs.b: Quantitative is measured by numbers, Qualitative picks a preset level, Conduct is scored with a behavior criteria set. A missing tab means that module is off.

edit.b: The screen is view-only by default; click here to open the fields.

reset.b: Returns the whole scale to the system default, overwriting every level you set.

max.b: The top score of a quantitative KPI. Changing it mid-cycle puts scored and upcoming periods on different scales.

levels.b: Each level has a name, a score threshold and a color. Scores at or above a threshold fall in that level; higher levels win.

edit.b: Click to edit level names, values and BSC %.

reset.b: Returns the levels to the default set, overwriting what you entered.

guide.b: Value is the converted score used by the matrix; BSC % is the completion used for BSC scoring.

levels.b: Reviewers pick exactly these level names. Use the words your company already uses so scoring stays consistent.

sets.b: Each set is assigned to one or more cycles; unassigned cycles use the default set. Open a set to edit criteria and weights.

groups.b: Group criteria. With groups, a criterion weight is % within its group and the groups add up to 100%.

addSet.b: Create a new set for cycles with different criteria. Old sets stay as they are for scored cycles.

help.b: Opens the explanation of how conduct criteria sets are assigned and scored.

reset.b: Returns the default set to 4 criteria at 25% each.

guide.b: Rows are behavior score, columns are KPI completion %. A rating appears only when the person has both axes.

table.b: Follow the row for behavior score and the column for KPI %; the cell where they meet is the rating.

edit.b: Rename the axes and bands, add rows or columns and fill in cell values.

reset.b: Returns the matrix to the default table.

levels.b: Rating levels from high to low — these are the names you pick when writing conditions.

profiles.b: Each profile is a rule set. A unit gets the first level from the top whose conditions it all meets.

add.b: Create a separate profile for a group of units; child units inherit it.

which.b: Open to review which unit follows which profile. Always keep a default profile.

help.b: Opens the explanation of unit rating profiles.

section.b: Each row is the code pattern for one object type, such as OKR objectives or BSC scorecards.

auto.b: When on, codes are generated from the pattern on creation.

manual.b: When on, the creator can still edit the generated code.

token.b: Click a part to insert it into the pattern, such as the year or a sequence number. Hover for an explanation.

tabs.b: A period is one round of submitting and scoring, usually monthly. A cycle groups periods into an overall result; ratings and rewards are by cycle.

stats.b: How many cycles the organization has and how many periods are grouped into them.

add.b: Pick the cycle type and date range, then group periods into it.

search.b: Type a cycle name to filter.

more.b: Filter by cycle type and date range.

table.b: The Periods column shows how many periods the cycle groups. A cycle with 0 periods has nothing for cycle evaluation to sum up.

edit.b: The button is dimmed for a locked cycle. A cycle locks only when the root unit's cycle evaluation is finalized.

history.b: See who locked or reopened the cycle and when.

stats.b: Total number of periods in the organization.

add.b: Set the name, period type, start and end date. Staff can submit only within that range.

search.b: Type a period name to filter.

table.b: Each row shows its cycle, dates and submission reminder.

edit.b: Shortening the end date of a running period immediately blocks people who have not submitted.

delete.b: A period in a locked cycle cannot be edited or deleted.

add.b: Create the Objective first, then add the Key Results that measure it.

list.b: Objective progress is calculated from its Key Results.

addKr.b: Add a quantitative Key Result to this objective. A KR linked to a KPI follows that KPI.

edit.b: Change the name, dates or owning unit of the objective.

import.b: Import many objectives and KRs at once from an Excel file.

tree.b: Scorecards from the company down to departments. Open a branch to edit items and weights and cascade them down.

card.b: Click to open its items, cascade coverage and period results. The card's menu switches between parallel and official scoring.

add.b: Create a scorecard for a cycle and a unit, then add items under the four perspectives.

import.b: Import a full scorecard with weights, or just the item catalog.

policy.b: Recognized score cap and the rule that KPIs must link to BSC.

tabs.b: Reward requests and Budgets to award points; Programs and Check-ins run automatically; Certificate templates; Gifts and Redemption requests.

filters.b: Pending approval is your work; the other statuses are for looking back.

award.b: Pick people, enter points and a reason. The reason shows on the activity feed for everyone.

ai.b: K.AI reviews pending requests and suggests approving or rejecting.

table.b: Within budget it takes effect at once; over budget it waits here for approval.

note.b: People with a budget award points immediately; going over turns it into a request awaiting approval.

add.b: Pick the manager, points, maximum per award and the period.

table.b: The progress bar shows how much is used. Expired budgets do not renew automatically.

note.b: Programs do not run on a schedule: click Run, pick a period or cycle, preview the ranking, then award.

add.b: Define the rule: who reaches the top of a period or cycle gets how many points.

table.b: Points from programs come from the shared fund, not from a manager's budget.

run.b: Pick the period or cycle, adjust tiers for this run if needed, then award.

note.b: Staff click it on My points; points go straight to their wallet.

stats.b: Today's check-ins and points awarded this month — check them before raising points per check-in.

form.b: Turn the feature on or off, points per check-in and the streak cycle.

milestones.b: Extra points when staff check in enough days in a row.

intro.b: Without templates the print screen still offers six designs; templates here carry your company's logo and signature.

add.b: Design your company's own certificate.

edit.b: Change the wording, logo or signature.

add.b: Enter name, image, point price and stock — exactly what staff see in the Gift shop.

urbox.b: Pick ready-made vouchers instead of entering items one by one.

table.b: At 0 stock the item is sold out. To retire an item, edit its stock instead of deleting it.

filters.b: Separate what awaits delivery from what is done.

table.b: Points were deducted when the employee redeemed; requests wait here for you to confirm delivery.

retry.b: For a voucher that failed to issue, click to ask again and fetch the code.

reject.b: Cancels the request and returns the points to the employee's wallet.

tabs.b: People balances for lookup, Configuration for the receiving account and rate, SePay reconciliation to match transfers.

stats.b: Holding is money topped up but not yet converted to points — what the organization owes staff.

filters.b: Search by name or email, filter by unit.

table.b: Click a wallet to see all of that person's movements.

bank.b: Account number and bank used to build the VietQR code. Without them staff cannot create a top-up.

rate.b: Money per 1 point. Past transactions keep the rate of their time.

limits.b: Limit per top-up and how long the QR code stays valid.

receipt.b: Details printed on the receipt sent to staff after a top-up.

status.b: Lists what is still missing before staff can top up.

preview.b: A sample conversion table at the rate you entered.

sepay.b: Link SePay so transfers arrive and match top-ups automatically.

status.b: Green means balanced; yellow means unmatched transactions or a wallet out of line with the ledger.

scope.b: To handle shows only unmatched transactions; full history is for looking up old ones.

table.b: Each row is one transfer received from SePay.

handle.b: Match a transaction to the right top-up by hand when the transfer note was wrong.

mine.b: Your own AI tokens for chatting with K.AI, separate from the pool you split among others.

pool.b: How much is left to split. With a pool of 0 you cannot allocate to anyone.

delegation.b: When on, unit heads can split tokens among their people, taken from their own quota.

people.b: Find people, filter by role and set the monthly quota. Once used up, K.AI stops answering until next month.

settings.b: Managers click "Ask AI to preview" when reviewing; AI reads the submission and evidence files and suggests a score. AI never records a score itself.

toggle.b: When off, the ask-AI button disappears from everyone's review screen.

weights.b: The suggested score combines several parts; adjust each part's share here.

criteria.b: Each unit applies one policy document; a child unit without one uses its parent's.

upload.b: Pick a Word, PDF or Excel file and a unit; AI extracts criteria for you to approve and apply.

report.b: Compares AI scores with finalized manager scores for the period. The goal is a small gap, mostly within ±5 points.

intro.b: The KPIs group is about setting and approving KPIs. The Evaluation group is scoring by period, then summing up by cycle. A red number on a card is work waiting for you.

kpi-criteria.b: Create, assign and submit KPIs for approval. KPIs not yet approved do not count toward results.

kpi-criteria-pending.b: KPIs waiting for you at the current step of the approval chain.

kpi-adjustments-pending.b: Requests to change a target, weight or stop a KPI mid-period; each has 24 hours to be handled.

submissions-org-unit.b: Approve submissions and score each person for a period.

cycle-evaluation.b: Sum the periods of a cycle into an overall score and finalize ratings. Finalizing at the root unit locks the cycle.

feedback360.b: Campaigns collecting managers', peers' and direct reports' views on each person.

stats.b: Total KPIs, how many are drafts and how many are pending approval for the current filters.

add.b: Opens the KPI form. The "Create a KPI" guide at the end of this one walks through each field.

import.b: Create many KPIs at once from an Excel file; the dialog has instructions and a template.

submitAi.b: K.AI checks the weights and submits the drafts of the selected unit and period for you, after you confirm.

period.b: Every figure on the page follows the selected period.

type.b: Filter quantitative or qualitative, parent, regular, bonus or inverse KPIs.

sort.b: By creation date, name, weight or target.

more.b: Filter by creation date, BSC item, or OKR objective and key result.

search.b: Type a KPI or person name.

view.b: Expand or collapse all groups, and switch between table and card view.

tabs.b: Draft is not submitted; Pending approval is going through the chain; Returned needs fixing and resubmitting.

list.b: Grouped by unit and person. The group header shows whether the total weight has reached 100%.

rowMenu.b: View, edit, submit, cascade or add a child KPI depending on status.

stats.b: Waiting for me is your work right now; Approved and Returned are for looking back.

ai.b: K.AI reviews the KPIs waiting for you and suggests approving or returning them.

period.b: Shows only KPIs of the selected period.

search.b: Search by KPI, unit or person name.

tabs.b: Pending is what waits for you at the current step of the chain.

table.b: With final approval permission, approving finalizes it; otherwise the KPI moves up to the next approver.

personApprove.b: Approve all of this person's pending KPIs at once.

view.b: Open the KPI to see figures, source and approval history before deciding.

approve.b: Approve your step. Only the holder of the current step can click it.

reject.b: Send the KPI back to its creator with a reason so they can fix it.

bulk.b: Approve every selected KPI at once.

stats.b: Requests pending, approved and rejected. Each request has 24 hours to be handled.

ai.b: K.AI reviews pending requests and suggests how to handle them.

period.b: Shows only requests of the selected period.

tabs.b: Pending is your work; the other tabs are for looking back.

table.b: Each row is a request to change a target, weight or stop a KPI, with a reason.

view.b: Read the reason and compare old and proposed figures before deciding.

approve.b: Accept the change; the KPI updates as requested.

reject.b: Keep the KPI as it is and note the reason for the requester.

bulk.b: Approve or reject every selected request at once.

stats.b: People, submissions pending approval and people already evaluated in the period.

search.b: Type a name to find someone quickly.

aiBatch.t: Ask AI to preview the whole unit
aiBatch.b: AI reads the submissions of everyone you can score, in the background; suggested scores are ready when you review.

aiApprove.b: K.AI reviews pending submissions and suggests scores for you to confirm.

aiRemind.b: K.AI finds who has not submitted and drafts a reminder.

table.b: People with pending submissions come first. The Reviewer column shows who scores each person.

score.b: Opens this person's scoring form: approve each submission and give scores.

viewEval.b: Look at the scored form again.

next.b: Once the period is scored, move on to the next step of the flow, usually cycle evaluation.

unit.b: Pick the unit to sum up. Without a unit and a cycle the screen stays empty.

cycle.b: Pick the cycle; the cycle score averages the periods in it.

stats.b: The unit's average scores for the cycle and its rating, marked provisional or finalized.

flow.b: Each step's status and buttons sit inside that step. Finalizing at the root unit locks the whole cycle; child units finalizing do not.

table.b: Each row shows period scores by the manager, the cycle rating and the final cycle score.

view.b: Open this person's period scores and add comments.

export.b: Export the whole cycle score table to a file.

send.b: Email the cycle evaluation results to each employee.

ai.b: K.AI checks the periods, builds the score table and waits for your confirmation.

create.b: Pick who is reviewed; the system suggests reviewers from the org tree.

filters.b: See draft, running or ended campaigns.

list.b: Each card shows the due date and forms submitted. Peer and direct-report forms are anonymous.

intro.b: The Work group holds your KPIs, submissions, evaluations and requests you sent. The Wallet group keeps reward points and real money apart. A red dot on a card is work waiting for you.

my-kpi.b: The KPIs you hold, grouped by period. Submit reports and self-assess from here.

my-okr.b: Objectives and key results your KPIs contribute to.

my-bsc.b: The BSC scorecards of your unit and the units above it.

my-submissions.b: Result reports you submitted and their approval status.

evaluations.b: Your evaluation results per period and your self-assessments.

my-adjustments.b: Requests you sent to change a target, weight or stop a KPI.

my-conduct.b: Conduct form: you self-score, your manager scores.

my-feedback360.b: 360 forms to fill in for colleagues, and your 360 report.

my-rewards.b: Reward point balance, check-in, gift shop and point history.

my-cash-wallet.b: Money balance, top-ups and conversion to points.

ai.b: K.AI summarizes this cycle's KPIs and your expected score.

search.b: Type a KPI name to filter.

view.b: Switch between table and card view.

table.b: Each block is a period; each row shows target, weight and progress.

submit.b: Opens the form to submit results for this KPI, with evidence files.

adjust.b: Ask your manager to change the target, weight or stop the KPI.

selfEval.b: When the period ends, click to score yourself before your manager does.

objective.b: Click to open its key results; the "You contribute" line shows which of your KPIs feed it.

search.b: Search by objective or key result name.

analytics.b: Go to Statistics for progress charts.

manage.b: Go to OKR setup if you can manage it.

scorecard.b: The BSC scorecard in view. Upper-level scorecards are for reference only; your BSC score uses the one attached to your own unit.

perspective.b: The items of this perspective with their weights and results.

search.b: Type an item name to filter.

analytics.b: Go to Statistics for detailed BSC scores.

manage.b: Go to BSC setup if you can manage it.

add.b: Pick a KPI and enter the result, with evidence files.

tabs.b: Draft is not sent; Pending awaits your manager; Returned needs fixing and resubmitting.

drafts.b: A shortcut to submissions you saved as drafts but have not sent.

list.b: Each row is one submission with its result and approval status.

edit.b: Reopen the draft to change figures or add files.

send.b: Send the draft to your manager. Once sent it can no longer be edited.

add.b: Opens the self-assessment form for a finished period.

selfNow.b: Appears when a period just ended and you have not scored yourself.

table.b: Each row shows your self-score, the manager score and the rating.

view.b: Opens the full evaluation form with the manager's comments.

add.b: Pick a KPI and ask to change its target, weight or stop it. Your manager has 24 hours to respond.

list.b: Track which requests are pending, approved or rejected.

target.b: Pick a period or cycle to open the conduct form.

sheet.b: Each row is a criterion: your column is for self-scoring, the manager column is scored by your manager.

export.b: Exports the form to a file.

ai.b: K.AI reads your form: self-score, manager score and criteria still missing evidence.

waiting.b: 360 forms you need to fill in for others. Peer and direct-report forms are anonymous.

reports.b: How others rated you, once the campaign has ended.

balance.b: Reward points you have to spend on gifts.

checkin.b: Click every day to earn points; consecutive days earn a bonus.

tabs.b: Gift shop, point history, certificates and redemption requests.

shop.b: Each card shows the point price and how many points you still need. An empty shop means no gifts have been added yet.

redeem.b: Click to redeem; points are deducted at once and the request awaits delivery.

history.b: Every time you earned or spent points.

certificates.b: Certificates attached to the rewards you received; it stays empty until a reward comes with one.

redemptions.b: Track whether redeemed gifts are awaiting delivery or received.

redeemView.b: Instant gifts come with a code (voucher) — click to view and copy it.

redeemCancel.b: A request still awaiting delivery can be cancelled; the points go back to your wallet.

certPrint.b: Opens the certificate for that reward to print or save as PDF.

balance.b: Money you topped up and have not converted to points.

topup.b: Create a top-up order and transfer using the VietQR code.

tabs.b: Convert to points, top-up history and transaction history.

convert.b: Turn wallet money into reward points at the company rate. Points never convert back to money.

topups.b: Orders you created; unpaid ones can be reopened.

history.b: Every money movement in your wallet.

convertRate.b: How much money buys one point. Points arrive in your points wallet right after converting.

convertPoints.b: Type the points; the box beside it shows the money to be deducted.

convertCost.b: Turns red when the wallet cannot cover it, with a line saying how much is missing.

convertMax.b: Fills in the most points your current balance can buy.

convertSubmit.b: Deducts money and adds points straight away. Points never convert back to money.

topupStatus.b: Awaiting transfer, received, expired or cancelled.

topupReceipt.b: View the receipt of an order whose money arrived.

topupResume.b: For a pending order, reopens the QR code and transfer description.

ledgerType.b: Top-up, conversion to points, received or adjusted.

ledgerExplain.b: The details of the transaction, e.g. the rate used when converting to points.

intro.b: Three views: your own results, the unit you manage and comparison between units, then the BSC scorecard. With OKR on, the first two cards show objectives instead of KPIs.

my-objectives.b: Your objectives and key results over time.

my.b: Your own KPI results: trends and details per KPI.

subordinate.b: Objectives of the unit you manage and each person's progress.

summary.b: Where the unit you lead stands: overall figures, trends, people ranking.

drilldown.b: Put units side by side: ratings, matrix, cascades.

bsc.b: Scores per BSC item, the balance radar and comparison with system scores.

intro.b: Progress of the objectives and key results you contribute to, for the time range set in each tile.

ai.b: Ask K.AI about the figures in this view.

intro.b: Your own KPI results. If a chart is empty, check the tile's time range first — usually it is a period nobody has submitted in.

ai.b: Ask K.AI about the figures in this view.

intro.b: Objectives of the unit you manage, each person's progress and child unit performance.

ai.b: Ask K.AI about the figures in this view.

intro.b: Overall progress, trends, people ranking and risk points of the unit you lead.

ai.b: K.AI compares the ranks of child units between the two latest evaluation periods.

intro.b: Put units side by side to see which department lags as a whole and which people pull the rest down.

ai.b: K.AI points out the child units whose self-scores differ most from manager scores.

sidebar.b: Pick the unit branch to compare; the tiles on the right follow.

intro.b: Scores per item, the four-perspective balance radar and comparison of BSC scores with system scores.

ai.b: Ask K.AI about the figures in this view.

add.b: Opens the library to add charts to this view. The layout is saved for your account only.

cell.b: Hover for details; click a row or bar to drill down where the chart allows it.

drag.b: Hold the dotted handle to drag the tile; drag a corner or edge to resize. Letting go saves it.

menu.b: Has Settings, Copy image, Pin to overview, Move up/down, Change width and Remove from page.

config.b: Unit, time range and display are set per tile — there is no page-wide filter.

intro.b: Ask in plain language about performance, objectives or people. K.AI sees only the data you are allowed to see.

starter.b: Not sure what to ask? Click a suggestion to start.

composer.b: Type your question; pin evidence files if you want K.AI to read them too. Shift + Enter for a new line.

send.b: Sends the question. Conversations keep their thread, so you can follow up with "what about department B" without restating the context.

sidebar.b: Reopen earlier conversations to keep asking.

new.b: Start a fresh thread with no prior context.

quota.b: K.AI uses your monthly token quota; once used up it stops answering until next month. Check figures K.AI summarizes against Statistics before putting them in a report.

intro.b: To-dos tied to KPIs: ones you own, follow or assign. Click a task to open details, comments and subtasks.

views.b: Assigned to me, Following, Created by me, Delegated, Done, and tasks per KPI.

create.b: Create a task with an owner, due date and linked KPI. Shortcut: N.

mode.b: Switch views: list to review, Kanban to drag by status, Calendar to see due dates.

group.b: Group tasks by status, due date, owner or KPI.

sort.b: Change the order of the list.

filter.b: Filter by status, due date, priority or period.

search.b: Type a task name to find it quickly.

quickAdd.b: Type a task name and press Enter to create it right in the list.

intro.b: Personal, unit and company documents in one place. K.AI reads exactly what each person may see.

new.b: Write a document or spreadsheet online, upload files, or create a folder.

nav.b: Home has recent and pinned documents; the Drive group is split by scope.

mine.b: Your personal documents; only people you share with can see them.

unit.b: Shared documents of the unit you belong to.

company.b: Company-wide documents such as policies and processes. K.AI relies on these for company questions.

requests.b: Requests to move a document to a wider scope, awaiting approval.

trash.b: Deleted documents stay here for a while before they are gone for good; they can be restored.

main.b: Folders and documents of the selected item. Click a document to view, share or see versions.

usersForm.title: Add a person — field by field

add.b: This button opens the account form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: Fill in every field marked * and click Create. The guide is running, so the form is not sent anywhere.

name.b: Shown in every list, evaluation sheet and email sent to this person.

code.b: Optional. Use your internal code so Excel import/export and other systems line up.

email.b: Used to sign in and receive notifications. One email belongs to one account.

password.b: At least 8 characters. Suggest generates a strong one, the eye icon shows it; the bar below rates its strength.

unit.b: Where this person works. The unit decides who approves their KPIs and whose data they can see.

role.b: Only roles that fit the level of the chosen unit are listed. The role carries this person's permissions.

submit.b: Click Create to save. The new person signs in with this email and password; click their row later to edit.

rolesForm.title: Create a role — field by field

add.b: This button opens the role form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: A role has a name, a management tier and a position within the tier. Permissions come in the next guide.

name.b: The name everyone sees, e.g. "Marketing Manager". System roles can only be renamed.

level.b: Which tier of the unit tree the role belongs to (from Ranks). People only get roles of their unit's tier.

rank.b: Head, Deputy or Member. Each tier has at most one Head and one Deputy role; the Head holds the unit's KPI approval step.

submit.b: Saves the role. Then open the role row menu › Permissions to choose what it can do.

drawer.b: Opened from a role's menu › Permissions. The guide opens it for the first role in the list.

defaults.b: Suggests the standard set for the position (director, head, deputy, staff). You preview it before it is added.

search.b: Type a permission code or group, e.g. KPI or APPROVE, to filter.

group.b: Permissions are grouped by resource (KPI, Submission…). x/y shows how many in the group are selected.

groupToggle.b: Selects or clears every permission in the group at once.

item.b: Click to turn it on or off. Hover to read what it allows.

save.b: Changes only apply after you click Save; Cancel discards them.

hierarchyBtn.b: This button opens a dialog that sets the standard permissions for EVERY role at once, by each role's position.

legend.b: Green means full access, amber partial, × none.

matrix.b: Each row is a permission, each column a role. Read down a column to see what that role will get.

apply.b: Overwrites the current permissions of every role with the matrix. Only use it to reset permissions from scratch.

orgForm.title: Add a unit — field by field

form.b: Opened from the add-child button on the chart, or Create root unit. The guide opens the form for a child of the root unit.

logo.b: Optional. Shown on the chart and the unit card.

parent.b: The parent unit and level of the new unit, filled in from where you clicked add.

name.b: Shown on the chart, in reports and in the approval chain.

code.b: A short unique code, used for Excel import/export.

type.b: What kind of unit it is, e.g. Department, Division, Team.

status.b: Active or discontinued. Defaults to active.

relation.b: Line, Advisory or Supervisory. It only changes the line style on the chart; approvals and visibility still follow the parent unit.

contact.b: The unit's shared email and phone, optional.

location.b: Province/city, ward and street address. The pickers are searchable.

roles.b: Limits which roles can be given to people in this unit. Roles that don't fit the level are locked, with the reason.

submit.b: Saves the unit. It appears on the chart straight away.

open.b: This button switches the ranks block into edit mode. Click it or press Next.

note.b: Changing the structure affects units already created, so settle it early.

row.b: Each row is one tier of the unit tree; the number is the level (1 is the top).

name.b: What units on this tier are called, e.g. Branch, Department, Team.

managerTitle.b: What the head of a unit on this tier is called, e.g. Director, Head of department.

order.b: The arrows move a level; the bin deletes it. At least 2 levels are always required.

add.b: Adds a new tier at the end.

save.b: Saves it; Cancel next to it discards every change.

delegationsForm.title: Create a delegation — field by field

add.b: This button opens the delegation form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: Lets someone also manage units outside their existing scope.

delegate.b: The person receiving the delegation. The list is grouped by unit; type to search.

units.b: Pick one or more. Units above the delegate's level are hidden, with a note saying how many.

subtree.b: On: the delegation covers every child unit too. Off: only the units you picked.

leader.b: Turn on when the delegate must do the head's work, such as conduct scoring.

expires.b: Leave empty for no expiry. The delegation lasts through the whole chosen day.

reason.b: A note for whoever reads it later, e.g. "Team lead on a business trip".

submit.b: Saves the delegation. Revoke it any time from the list below.

open.b: Every KPI still open has this button. Click it or press Next to open the request form for the first KPI.
When a period has ended and you haven't self-assessed, its group header shows this button. Click it or press Next to open the sheet.

dialog.b: Ask to change a KPI's numbers or stop it; the request goes through the approval chain like a new KPI.

note.b: You can change the target or minimum, or ask to stop the KPI. Who approves is shown in the chain after sending.

mode.b: Choose to edit the numbers, or to stop the KPI altogether.

numbers.b: Leave a box as it is to keep that value. The unit is shown inside the box.

reason.b: Required. Say exactly why the change is needed — approvers read this first.

submit.b: Sends it for approval. Follow it under My adjustment requests.

dialog.b: You score your own period before your manager does.

context.b: Pick the period to assess. Only periods where you have KPIs are listed.

score.b: The system score comes from your KPI results; you can change it, and the restore button returns to it.

evidence.b: Attach evidence and write a few lines about your period.

submit.b: Sends the sheet to your manager. After sending it is view-only.

myAdjForm.title: Send an adjustment request — step by step

add.b: This button opens the picker for the KPI to adjust. Click it or press Next.

picker.b: Only KPIs that can still be adjusted are listed: period not over and no request already pending.

item.b: Click a KPI to open the request form for it. KPIs with a pending request are greyed out.

add.b: This button opens the self-assessment sheet. Click it or press Next to see it.

redeemForm.title: Redeem a gift — step by step

open.b: Every gift has this button. Click it or press Next to open the redeem dialog for the first gift.

gift.b: Name, points, value and how many are left.

quantity.b: How many to redeem; the points deducted follow the quantity.

balance.b: Points you have, points to be deducted and what remains. If you are short, it says by how much.

submit.b: Redeems and deducts points. If you are short on points but your cash wallet covers it, the button buys the missing points first.

topupForm.title: Top up the wallet — step by step

add.b: This button opens the top-up dialog. Click it or press Next to see it.

dialog.b: Top up by bank transfer; money arrives once the bank confirms it.

amount.b: Enter how much to top up, within the minimum – maximum shown below.

quick.b: Click a preset amount instead of typing.

submit.b: Creates the top-up order with a QR code and transfer description. Keep the description exact, or the money won't reach the wallet automatically.

dialog.b: Click a KPI name in the list to open this dialog. The guide opens the first KPI in the list.

facts.b: Target, minimum, weight, frequency and the KPI's deadlines.

assignees.b: Who will receive this KPI. Check before approving.

chain.b: The approval steps from the KPI's unit up to the root: which are done and who is up next.

reject.b: Opens a reason box. The KPI goes back to its creator with the reason; resubmitting starts the chain over.

approve.b: Approves your step. If there are steps above, the KPI moves on to that step holder instead of starting.

reviewAdj.title: View and approve an adjustment request

dialog.b: Click a request in the list to open this dialog. The guide opens the first request.

reason.b: Why the requester needs the KPI changed.

compare.b: Each metric side by side: the current value and the requested one.

reject.b: Opens a note box, then rejects; the requester is notified with the note.

approve.b: Opens a note box (and compensation rate, if any), then approves. Adjustments always go through the whole chain.

dialog.b: Click Score on a person's row to open it. The guide opens the first person's sheet (a specific period must be selected).

kpis.b: Each submission with result, target and system score; the box beside it lets you re-score if needed.

score.b: The period total (defaults to the sum of your scores), plus conduct and matrix rating when enabled.

comments.b: Comments from levels that scored before you, and your own comment box.

submit.b: Approves all submissions and saves the official result. Locked while returned submissions await resubmission.

cycleEval.title: Score, finalize and send the cycle evaluation

unitScore.b: Opened from the step bar at the top, at the calibration step. By default the unit score is the members' average.

unitSummary.b: The current score and whether it is the average or a manual score.

unitManual.b: Type a score different from the average; a reason is then required. The button next to it goes back to the average.

unitSlider.b: Drag to pick a score; the rating label follows.

unitSave.b: Only enabled once the score has changed.

finalize.b: Opened from the finalize button on the step bar: the unit score to be locked and any warnings first.

finalizeComment.b: Optional, saved with the locked result.

finalizeUnfinished.b: Choose how to handle each unfinished KPI before locking; until all are chosen you cannot lock.

finalizeConfirm.b: Locks the unit's cycle result. Finalizing the root unit also locks the whole cycle.

send.b: Opened from Send evaluations. Search and pick who gets the results email.

sendList.b: Tick people one by one, or use select all above.

sendSubmit.b: Emails the results to the selected people.

f360Form.title: Create a 360 campaign — field by field

add.b: This button opens the 360 campaign form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

purpose.b: Development only, or counted toward the rating. If counted, a KPI cycle is required.

cycle.b: The cycle the 360 result is attached to.

window.b: Open date and deadline, suggested from the cycle. Click Adjust to change them.

questions.b: Competencies and questions, each competency weighted. You can copy questions from an earlier campaign.

process.b: Whether reviewees rate themselves, nominate extra raters, and can see their own report.

advanced.b: Anonymity, automation (AI summary, auto-close), weights by group and limits for automatic rater selection.

submit.b: The campaign is saved as a draft; add reviewees before launching it.

newSub.title: Submit a result report — field by field

intro.b: This page records what you achieved on a KPI, with an explanation and evidence, and sends it to your manager. The guide goes field by field and sends nothing.

kpi.b: Pick the KPI to report on. Opened from a KPI's Submit button, it is already selected.

actual.b: The number you achieved (for a qualitative KPI, pick a level). The system score compares it with the target.

note.b: How you got there and anything notable — this is what the approver reads.

files.b: Drop images, PDF, Word or Excel files, or pick existing files from the document library. Evidence makes the report more credible.

side.b: Target, minimum, weight, period and how many times you have submitted — to check against while filling in.

draft.b: Keeps it to finish later. Drafts can be edited any time; once sent for approval they cannot.

submit.b: Asks once more, then sends it to your manager for approval.

cycleForm.title: Create a cycle — field by field

add.b: This button opens the cycle form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: A cycle groups several periods for one end-of-cycle evaluation, e.g. a year of four quarters.

mode.b: Set the dates first and pick periods inside them, or pick periods first and let the dates wrap them. Switching keeps what you typed.

name.b: The name everyone sees, e.g. "2026" or "H1 2026".

type.b: Month, quarter, half-year or year. It sets the standard end date; if yours differs, the form asks before saving.

evalMode.b: Quantitative (KPI figures), qualitative or both. Without qualitative enabled, only quantitative is offered.

dates.b: Start and end of the cycle. When you pick periods first, these are derived from them.

periods.b: Tick the periods that belong to the cycle now, instead of editing each period later.

description.b: The overall goal of the cycle, optional.

submit.b: Saves the cycle. A cycle only locks when the root unit's cycle evaluation is finalized; there is no separate lock button.

periodForm.title: Create a period — field by field

add.b: This button opens the period form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: A period is the window in which KPIs are assigned and submitted, e.g. October or Q4.

name.b: Shown in filters and on every KPI of the period.

type.b: Week, month, quarter… The end date is suggested from the start date and type.

cycle.b: Optional. Attach the period to a cycle so its results roll up into the end-of-cycle evaluation.

dates.b: Start and end of the period. Its KPIs can only be submitted inside this window.

reminder.b: When the submission reminder goes out; defaults to halfway through the period.

submit.b: Saves the period. It appears straight away in the period filters of KPI screens.

objectiveForm.title: Create an OKR objective — field by field

add.b: This button opens the objective form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: An objective is what the organization wants to achieve; the numbers live in its key results.

name.b: The objective's name and code. The code can be issued by the organization's code rule.

dates.b: Start and end of the objective.

units.b: Units pursuing the objective. With several units, each key result splits a % across them.

bsc.b: Optionally link the objective to an item of a BSC scorecard.

submit.b: Saves the objective. Then add key results right on its row.

krForm.title: Add a key result — field by field

add.b: This button on each objective opens the KR form. The guide opens it for the first objective.

form.b: A KR is the number that measures the objective. KPIs can use a KR as their source.

name.b: The KR's name, e.g. "Online revenue". The code can be issued automatically.

description.b: How it is measured or where the data comes from, optional.

numbers.b: Unit of measure, current value and target value. Progress is computed from these.

allocation.b: Only shown when the objective has several units. The boxes must add up to 100%.

submit.b: Saves the KR to the objective.

bscForm.title: Create a BSC scorecard — field by field

add.b: This button opens the scorecard form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

applyScope.b: By cycle: pick one cycle and all its periods apply. By period: tick each period.

periods.b: When the scorecard is in force. This box follows the Apply by choice.

scope.b: Units that use this scorecard. A unit without its own scorecard gets no BSC score; cascade down to follow the company one.

vision.b: The central strategy every item serves, optional.

emptyPolicy.b: How to score an item that has no KPIs yet; each option explains the effect.

items.b: Tick items to include them; the ticked weights must add up to 100%.

split.b: Spreads the weight evenly across the ticked items.

area.b: Items are grouped by the four BSC perspectives (financial, customer…). The pencil renames or recolors a perspective.

addItem.b: Creates a new item inside this perspective.

rowToggle.b: Click to add the item to the scorecard or remove it. Items assigned from above are locked.

rowWeight.b: The item's percentage of the scorecard total.

submit.b: Saves the scorecard. Quick create also offers Save as draft next to it.

add.b: This button opens the award form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: Pick people, points and a reason. Points go to their wallet to redeem gifts.

budget.b: Points you can still award in your budget and the cap per person per award.

people.b: Search and pick one or more recipients.

points.b: Points each person gets; the box next to it totals the group.

reason.b: Shown in the employee's points history, so be specific. With a certificate it is printed on it too.

certificate.b: Turn on to give a printable certificate, then choose the template.

submit.b: Over budget or without self-approval, the button becomes Send for approval and waits for a manager.

budgetForm.title: Grant a reward budget — field by field

add.b: This button opens the budget form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: A budget is how many points one person may award to others over a time range.

recipient.b: The person who will award points from this budget.

scope.b: By cycle, by period or a date range. A person has one budget at a time, so ranges must not overlap.

total.b: Points this person may award during the range.

max.b: The cap for one recipient in one award.

submit.b: Saves the budget. Later you cannot lower the total below what has been awarded.

programForm.title: Automatic reward program — field by field

add.b: This button opens the program form. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: A program ranks people by results and pays points by tier when a cycle/period ends.

applies.b: Every cycle/period (repeats) or one specific cycle/period, for one-off rewards such as year-end.

ranking.b: Cycle or period, and the metric used for ranking.

units.b: Rank across the company or within each unit.

tiers.b: Points per rank. Only defaults — each run can still be edited.

tie.b: Same rank same reward, or pay exactly that many people in a fixed order.

auto.b: On: points reach wallets when the cycle/period ends without anyone reviewing; you can still pay manually earlier.

submit.b: Saves the program. The run button on its row previews before paying.

giftForm.title: Add a gift — field by field

add.b: This button opens the gift form for the points shop. Click it or press Next to see the form.

form.b: Gifts are what employees redeem with reward points.

image.b: Upload the picture shown on the gift card in the shop.

name.b: The gift name and a few lines for whoever redeems it.

points.b: Points needed for one item and how many are left. Tick Unlimited if you don't need to count.

delivery.b: Handed over in person: the request waits until someone marks it handed over. Received instantly: done on redemption, e.g. a day off.

submit.b: Saves the gift. Untick On sale to hide it without deleting.

add.b: This button opens the certificate designer. Click it or press Next to see it.

name.b: Only shown in the template picker, not printed.

style.b: Start from a preset, then edit the text, colors and images below.

content.b: Lead-in, title, subtitle, body, footer, and switches to show the logo, organization name, points and reason.

signer.b: Name, title, signature/seal image, custom logo and background image. Backgrounds can be removed automatically.

flags.b: Make it the company default, or turn off In use to hide it from the picker.

preview.b: The certificate exactly as it will print, updated as you edit.

submit.b: Saves the template. It can be used straight away when awarding points with a certificate.

taskForm.title: Create a task — field by field

add.b: This button opens the new-task dialog. Click it or press Next to see it.

form.b: Every task belongs to one of the owner's KPIs, so its progress sits next to the target it serves.

name.b: Type a name, then Ctrl + Enter to create it quickly.

owner.b: Defaults to you. Assigning to someone else needs the assign permission, and only people in units you manage can be picked.

kpi.b: Required. Only the owner's KPIs that you can see are listed; changing the owner clears it.

due.b: The date, and optionally time, it must be done by.

priority.b: Used to sort and filter the task list.

more.b: Opens: who can see it (public within the KPI scope or private), description, and a checklist with one step per line.

submit.b: Creates the task and opens its details, where you add followers, reminders and recurrence.

docsCreate.title: Create a document, upload, create a folder

menu.b: The New button opens this menu: new document, new spreadsheet, upload document, new folder.

onlineTitle.b: Name it and click Create to open the online editor. New spreadsheet uses the same dialog.

onlineScope.b: Personal, Unit or Company. For Unit, also pick which unit. Inside a scope already, this box is hidden.

onlineSubmit.b: Creates an empty document and opens the editor.

uploadDrop.b: Drag and drop or click to pick a file. Its name is filled in as the title.

uploadTitle.b: The name shown in the library; tidy it up so it is easy to find.

uploadMeta.b: Who can see the document and what kind it is.

uploadDescription.b: A few lines on what it is for, optional.

uploadAi.b: On: K.AI reads the document when answering people in that scope. Off: it is still stored to view and download.

uploadSubmit.b: Uploads the file to the library.

folderScope.b: Which scope the folder belongs to; documents inside follow it.
